questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Lack of sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces your awareness, and impairs your judgment — just like alcohol and drugs do.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed through the zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and hazards.

questions.question: If pedestrians are crossing in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are crossing illegally, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: You may go through if it is safe and clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through if it is safe and clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go through the intersection. First check that the path is clear and yield to any pedestrians or traffic already in the intersection.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk. Wait until they finish crossing before you proceed.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It reduces alertness and concentration, slows reaction time, and reduces coordination.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, alcohol's effects will only go away by:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, showers, and exercise do not speed this up. One drink takes about one hour to wear off.

questions.question: If you arrive at an accident scene and your help is not needed, you should:

options.text: Stop and look out of curiosity.

questions.explanation: If you are not trained to help, keep driving. This prevents you from blocking emergency services and keeps you safe from other distracted drivers.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs impair driving ability, including tranquilizers, sedatives, marijuana, and over-the-counter medicines like cough syrups, cold tablets, and allergy medicine.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when gates are lowered or warning signs appear. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your safety belt and check that all passengers do the same before you start the engine.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians near your vehicle at all times. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the situation is.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming up ahead.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout:

options.text: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Press the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the accelerator and slow down gradually. Do not brake hard until the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming up at the next intersection.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists who are crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you:

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving at the same speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not speed up or brake. Keep a steady speed and let the other vehicle pass safely and merge back into your lane.

questions.question: Emergency crossovers on Tennessee interstates can be used by:

options.text: Anyone to make a U-turn when they miss their exit.
Anyone to turn around if no other cars are present.
Emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.
questions.explanation: In Tennessee, drivers cannot make U-turns on interstate highways. Emergency crossovers on interstates are only for emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews.

questions.question: When you see a blind person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until they are safely away from your vehicle.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are safely away from your vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop. Always give blind pedestrians the right of way.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus can turn.
Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.

questions.question: What should you do if you meet an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: When you meet an aggressive driver, the safest choice is to get out of their way. Do not try to compete with other drivers. Let them pass and avoid conflict.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep the same speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, slow down and look both ways. Listen for any trains and be ready to stop if you see one coming. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: When a school bus stops on your side of the road with red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: A school bus uses flashing red lights and a stop arm when picking up or dropping off students. You must stop and stay stopped until the red lights stop flashing. Never pass a school bus that is loading or unloading students.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas you cannot see when you get tired.
Areas of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show. When changing lanes, turn your head to look over your shoulder to check these blind spots.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood can affect your:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and your ability to control the car. This is true even if your blood alcohol level is below the legal limit. Drinking and driving is dangerous and illegal.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: That it is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other vehicles in that area. These signs are placed where it is not safe to pass, such as where you cannot see far enough ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals because bikes do not have turn signals. When a bicyclist holds their left arm straight out, they are signaling a left turn.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off the wet air and make it harder to see.

questions.question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Carefully pass at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Never pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. There may be pedestrians you cannot see. Stop behind the vehicle and only move when all pedestrians have safely crossed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign means traffic may be merging from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely into your lane.
